_comment: Charity walks on Blackbaud Luminate Online TeamRaiser, read by mapsee_ingest_luminate.py through the client API each charity's own event finder calls (CRTeamraiserAPI method=getTeamraisersByInfo, name=%%%, list_page_size=500): 8 requests a run across three hosts, at 2 s, with no request after --max-minutes. Every request carries the charity's own api_key, the one each publishes in its own finder page; Blackbaud's help says the key 'is not a secure password. You can include this key in a hidden field of a web form', and robots.txt on all three hosts has no rule touching /site/CRTeamraiserAPI (2026-10-11). Using another organisation's key is the owner's decision, recorded in `_decision`. The record publishes no course, so no route is read. Read the adapter's header before changing a rule.
_decision: SWITCHED ON by the owner on 2026-10-11. Asked whether to use the charities' published Blackbaud Luminate API keys, he answered: 'Yes use them, try to map the route so users can see where the event walks when clicking on the event.' So each request carries the key that charity publishes in its own event finder (ACS 'ACSAPI', Alzheimer's Association 'ALZADARDA', Komen 'pink') and is the finder's own call (getTeamraisersByInfo, name=%%%, the programme's event_type, 500 a page), made at 2 s under the production User-Agent after robots.txt; a 401/403/429 or a challenge ends that host's reads. The charities were NOT asked. The route: neither the API record nor the event pages publish a course anywhere (separate research, 2026-10-11), so none is read. Unlike the borrowed DICE key (docs/agents/curation-and-discovery.md), robots.txt does not refuse this path and Blackbaud documents the key as public. THE WAY BACK: rename this file to luminate_sources.json.pending-permission; the workflow step is guarded [ -f luminate_sources.json ], so it skips from the next run and no row is written or refreshed after it (rows already stored stay until their dates pass).
_measured: 2026-10-11, replaying that day's pulls (7 requests, made by the discovery run): Making Strides 175 records, Relay For Life 1,055, Walk to End Alzheimer's (event_type 'Walk 2026') 624, Komen 59. Within 180 days the adapter writes 435 rows (Strides 97, Relay 82, Alzheimer's 239, Komen 17); the Census batch plus the Alzheimer's pins place 396 of them (143 of 179 ACS, 238 of 239 Alzheimer's, 15 of 17 Komen). 253 say 'Free to join: there is no registration fee.' (all Alzheimer's rows, 14 Komen MORE THAN PINK walks), and ../mapsee migration 0227's free predicate tags all 253 free (the first draft's 'Free to register.' was tagged on 0). Paducah's 'AK' beside a Kentucky pin is written with no state.
_pause: Seconds between requests. One run is 7 requests across three hosts; nothing asks for a crawl-delay.
_placeholder_days: MM-DD a record is never written on: December 31 is the charities' fiscal year-end, where 189 of 1,055 Relay records and 36 of 175 Making Strides records sat on 2026-10-11 (tests, 'Venue Name', 'NO EVENT THIS YEAR.', and real chapters with no date yet).
